evidence: src/domain/product.ts: Product.reserve throws DomainError("INSUFFICIENT_STOCK", `Insufficient stock for product ${this.id}: requested ${quantity}, available ${this.available}`) when quantity > this.available.

src/domain/stock-allocation-service.ts: StockAllocationService.reserve repeats `if (line.quantity > product.availableQuantity)` and throws the identical INSUFFICIENT_STOCK error and message, instead of asking Product.

src/domain/stock-allocation-service.ts: the pre-check looks at each line on its own and ignores other lines for the same product, so Product.reserve can still throw partway through the second loop after some products have already been reserved and saved.
src/domain/order-status.ts and src/domain/order.ts: the transition rules (nextFulfilmentStatus, isCancellable) live in one place and Order uses them correctly.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module holds together as one ordering and stock domain. Order, OrderLine and the OrderStatus helpers make up the order aggregate. Product and ProductRepository make up the stock aggregate. StockAllocationService links the two. Every file uses DomainError, and the status-transition rules live only in order-status.ts, where Order uses them correctly.

The insufficient-stock invariant, however, is written twice. Product.reserve owns the check `quantity > this.available` and throws DomainError("INSUFFICIENT_STOCK", "Insufficient stock for product ...: requested ..., available ..."). StockAllocationService.reserve re-implements the same comparison against product.availableQuantity and builds the same error code and message itself. It does not ask Product, for example through a canReserve query. If the rule or its message changes, both places must be updated.

The duplicated check also has a gap. It looks at each line against the product's full available stock, so two lines for the same product can each pass while their total is too high. Product.reserve then throws after earlier lines in the loop have already reserved and saved stock. The pre-check is meant to make reservation all-or-nothing, and it fails to.

violations.message: StockAllocationService.reserve duplicates the insufficient-stock rule owned by Product.reserve. It re-implements the `quantity > available` check and copies the INSUFFICIENT_STOCK error and message, bypassing the Product aggregate. Product should expose a single check (for example, canReserve) that both use. The copied check also ignores other lines for the same product, so a reservation can partly succeed.
